summary:
H.J. Res. 90 is a Congressional Review Act joint resolution of disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code. Its sole operative provision provides that Congress disapproves the final guidance submitted by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission entitled “Commission Guidance Regarding the Listing of Voluntary Carbon Credit Derivative Contracts,” published at 89 Fed. Reg. 83378 (Oct. 15, 2024), and declares that the rule “shall have no force or effect.”

The measure does not amend any provision of the Commodity Exchange Act or any other section of the United States Code. It creates no new regulatory authority, compliance obligation, program, authorization of appropriations, or direct appropriation. It contains no exceptions, savings clauses, transition provisions, or separate effective-date provision; its operative legal effect would arise upon enactment as a joint resolution under the Congressional Review Act. The resolution is limited to congressional disapproval of the specified CFTC final guidance concerning the listing of voluntary carbon credit derivative contracts.
